properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 2:20PM EST until November 18 at 4:15PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
FFWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Miami-Dade County in southeastern Florida...

* Until 415 PM EST.

* At 220 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Homestead, Black Point, Homestead Miami Speedway, Homestead Base,
Princeton, Goulds, Cutler Bay, Homestead Bayfront Park and Palmetto
Bay.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Thursday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide
at 1049 PM tonight, 1104 AM Thursday, and 1041 Thursday night.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12
to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored
breakpoints along the coast from this afternoon through Friday
morning.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday.
These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will
enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide
varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast
and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

conditions.

infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the
drainages within Lafler, Castro, and Graves Canyons, as well as
drainages between Grimes and Castro Canyons.

Residents near the Plaskett burn area should prepare for potential
debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and Prewitt Creeks.

roadway flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 18 at 3:02AM PST until November 18 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 3 and 7
inches. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of the southern Oregon Cascades and Siskiyous,
including Crater Lake National Park, Sky Lakes Wilderness, and
Diamond Lake. This includes portions of highways 138, 230, and 62.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST this evening. A majority of accumulation
will occur this morning.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. The hazardous
conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening commutes.
Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

NWSheadline: WINTER WEATHER ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM PST THIS EVENING

* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by
excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following area, Southern Kenai Mtns. This
includes the city of Seward.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

may occur in poor drainage areas.

morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With
upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 4 inches

elevation. Rainfall rates of up to a quarter of an inch per hour
are possible between 3PM Wednesday through 3PM Thursday.

early Thursday morning, limiting precipitation amounts in lee of
the mountains for areas along the Seward Highway from roughly
Moose Pass and southward to Seward. Rainfall is on track to
decrease late Thursday afternoon. Prolonged heavy rain may lead
to areas of flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in
low-lying and poor drainage areas, and ponding of water on
roadways.
